name: @productbrain/mcp

tools.name: session
tools.description:
Start here. When the person says "Start my Product Brain session.", call start.

Session lifecycle, wrapup review, and work package facilitation.

- **start**: Begin a tracked write session for attribution. **This is the ONLY call that creates a session** — write tools (capture, entries action=update/accept, relations) require it. Its reply is the briefing; then `orient task="<what you are doing>"` loads the context for a task.
- **close**: End the current session. Records structured data (entries created, modified, relations). Run `session action=wrapup-review` before closing.
- **status**: Check current session — active or not, oriented, activity counts.
- **wrapup-review**: List this session's drafts with quality scores; accept each with entries action=accept. Run before close.
- **resume**: Load session state (work package data, linked entries, drafts) from an existing work package entry.

action.description: 'start': begin a tracked session. 'close': end the session and record activity. 'status': check current session state. 'wrapup-review': list this session's drafts before closing. 'resume': load session state from an existing work package entry.

betEntryId.description: For 'resume': work package entry ID. Required.

role.description: For 'start': role to act as this session, by the '<PREFIX>-<n>' id a start reply prints beside the role name — only needed if you hold more than one; the error lists your roles if omitted.

team.description: For 'start': the team the role is held in, by its 'TEAM-<n>' id — only needed with role, when you hold that role in more than one team; a refusal that names the way in prints it.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: entries
tools.description:
Write entries on the Chain: the entry lifecycle after capture. Reads live on `context`.

- **update**: Change fields on an existing entry (publishes whenever the entry is not draft — includes archived, not just accepted/active; autoPublish is accepted but ignored).
- **accept**: Accept a draft entry onto the Chain. Runs the contradiction preflight first.
- **move**: Relocate an entry to a different collection; pass canonicalKey too for an atomic move+retype.
- **verify**: Mark verified (lightweight, no scan — see `quality action=verify-chain`).
- **still-true**: confirm accuracy (the holder of the owning role; if that role is empty, the nearest seated Team Lead up the team tree).

Read entries with the read-only `context` tool: `context action=get entryId="..."`, `context action=search query="..."`, `context action=preflight`.

action.description: 'update': change fields on an existing entry (draft by default). 'accept': accept a draft entry onto the Chain. 'move': relocate an entry to a different collection (pass `canonicalKey` too for an atomic move+retype). 'verify': mark an entry as verified (lightweight — no codebase scan; see `quality action=verify-chain` for that). 'still-true': confirm accuracy (the holder of the owning role, else the nearest seated Team Lead) — distinct from 'verify'; no content, version, or updatedAt change.

entryId.description: Entry ID, e.g. '<PREFIX>-<n>'. Required for: update, accept, move, verify, still-true.

status.description: For 'update': draft|archived ONLY — 'accepted' is set via 'accept', never 'update'; 'active'/'deprecated' are legacy read-only words, refused on write. Workflow values use `workflowStatus` instead.

workflowStatus.description: For 'update': collection workflow state. Valid values are collection-specific and server-owned — discover via `collections action=describe`. Invalid values are rejected with the valid set.

data.description: For 'update': fields to update (merged with existing data).

canonicalKey.description: For 'update': semantic type (e.g. 'decision', 'tension'); only changeable on draft entries. For 'move': optional atomic move+retype target.

autoPublish.description: For 'update': accepted for backward compatibility but IGNORED — draft vs. published is decided by the entry's own accepted/active status, never by this flag.

changeReason.description: For 'update': Change reason — required when the update changes a promise field of an accepted entry. Recorded on the history event and the version.

changeNote.description: For 'update': short human-readable rationale for WHY this change was made. Surfaces in activity feed.

sourceRef.description: For 'update': URI or path of the source document backing this entry. Write-once.

sourceExcerpt.description: For 'update': verbatim excerpt from the source backing this entry's claims. Write-once.

steeringOverrideReason.description: For 'update'/'accept': typed override (≥12 chars) that clears a steering coherency block.

qualityOverrideReason.description: For 'update'/'accept': why (≥12 chars) to keep a spine text its quality checklist failed; recorded as an override with who wrote it.

response.description: Explicit response to an acknowledge-required coherency challenge.

entryId.description: Authorizing entry being linked/accepted (required for 'linked' and 'accepted-fix').

coherencyAcknowledgement.description: For 'update'/'accept': explicit response to a coherency challenge (standard/strict workspace modes).

preview.description: For 'accept': if true, validates the accept without writing — returns what would happen.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: relations
tools.description:
Create and delete relations between entries, each written only on request with exactly the verb you send. Read relations with the read-only `context action=find`.

The spine links, child to parent: A work package validates an accepted key result. A key result hangs on an accepted objective with part_of. An objective hangs on an accepted strategy with part_of. A strategy hangs on an accepted vision with part_of. A vision hangs on an accepted purpose with part_of.

action.description: 'create': link two entries. 'batch-create': create multiple relations (validates every item before writing any). 'delete': remove a relation.

type.description: Relation type, for create, delete and each batch-create item.

preview.description: For 'create': if true, checks the relation and writes nothing.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: context
tools.description:
Read the Chain. Every action is a read except incremental, which records the brief run it steers.

- **get**: Fetch a single entry by ID — full record with data, labels, relations, history.
- **batch**: Fetch multiple entries (max 20) in one call. Same shape as get per entry.
- **history**: Audit trail for an entry.
- **list**: Browse entries with optional filters (collection, status, tag, label). Use collections action=list first to discover slugs.
- **search**: Full-text search across entries. Scope by collection or filter by status.
- **find**: An entry's direct relations, incoming and outgoing. NOT full-text search (use search).
- **people**: The workspace's members: name, email, status, role. Max 200.
- **outcome**: A key result's derived view (current, progress, pace, staleness, recorded completion) with its objective and up to 5 sibling key results.
- **readings**: A key result's readings, newest first; superseded rows are marked with their replacement. Record one with `outcome action=record`.
- **accountable**: What a role owns, reports on, and who holds it.
- **preflight**: What an entry in a collection needs before you compose it. Saves nothing.
- **gather**: Three modes — (1) By entry: traverse the graph around a specific entry. (2) By task: load task-relevant governance, binding constraints, and supporting domain knowledge for a natural-language task. (3) Graph mode (entryId + mode='graph'): enhanced traversal with provenance paths.
- **build**: Structured build spec for any entry — data, related entries, business rules, glossary terms, chain refs. Use when starting a build. Requires active session.
- **neighborhood**: Typed graph neighborhood — blocking chain (what this blocks, 3 hops), dependency chain (what blocks this), parent context (sibling count), related tensions, staleness signal, isolation signal. Fast indexed lookups. Requires entryId.
- **changes**: Detect entries modified and relations created since a timestamp. Use for incremental updates instead of full traversal. Requires 'since' (ISO 8601). Returns grouped counts by collection. Cap: 200 entries.
- **chain**: Directed deep traversal along one relation type to depth 4. Use for dependency analysis, governance chains, strategic alignment. Requires entryId. Optional: direction (outgoing/incoming), relationType, maxHops (1-4). Cycle detection, fan-out cap 10/hop, total cap 100 nodes. Returns tree + edges.
- **cross-cut**: Structural aggregation — all relations of a given type across the workspace, grouped by source collection. Use to answer 'show me everything connected by part_of'. Requires 'relationType'. Cap: 500 entries.
- **incremental**: Delta since last brief run for a skill. Returns only entries changed since the skill's last brief, filtering out previously surfaced entries. Requires 'skill' parameter. Use for steering briefs that need incremental awareness.
- **brief**: Compound intelligence query composing multiple primitives. Requires 'briefType': 'steering' (7d changes + structure + delta + readiness), 'confidence' (7d changes + active work packages — tensions: use the pb CLI's `tensions list`), or 'delta' (changes since custom timestamp). Auto-records brief run for steering.
- **last-verified-brief**: Fetch the most recent verified brief snapshot for a (templateId, scopeKey) pair (absorbs `documents`). Use to build delta narratives.

action.description: 'get': one entry in full by ID. 'batch': up to 20 entries by ID. 'history': audit trail for an entry. 'list': browse entries with filters (accepted by default). 'search': full-text search across entries. 'find': an entry's direct relations (direction: incoming|outgoing|both, default both). 'people': the workspace's members with name, email and status. 'outcome': a key result's derived view, its objective and sibling key results. 'readings': its readings, newest first. 'accountable': what a role owns and who holds it. 'preflight': a collection's requirements. 'gather': assemble knowledge context (entry graph, task auto-load, journey mode, or graph mode). 'build': structured build spec for an entry. 'neighborhood': typed graph neighborhood for an entry — blocking chain, dependencies, parent context, tensions, staleness. 'changes': entries modified and relations created since a timestamp. Requires 'since' parameter. 'chain': directed traversal along one relation type to depth 4. Requires entryId. Optional: direction, relationType, maxHops (1-4). 'cross-cut': structural aggregation — all relations of a given type grouped by source collection. Requires 'relationType' parameter. 'incremental': delta since last brief run for a skill. Requires 'skill' parameter. Returns only entries changed since the skill's last brief. 'brief': compound intelligence query. Requires 'briefType' parameter: 'steering' (changes + structure + delta + readiness), 'confidence' (changes + active bets — use the pb CLI's `tensions list` for tensions), or 'delta' (changes + relations since timestamp). Optional 'since' for delta type. 'last-verified-brief': fetch the most recent verified brief snapshot for a (templateId, scopeKey) pair. Requires templateId and scopeKey.

entryId.description: For 'get'/'history'/'find'/'outcome'/'readings'/'build'/'neighborhood'/'chain': entry ID. For 'gather': optional (entry-graph mode).

collection.description: For 'list'/'search': collection slug, e.g. 'glossary', 'tracking-events'. Required for 'preflight'.

status.description: For 'list': defaults to accepted entries (active/accepted/current); use status='draft' to discover drafts. One lifecycle or category value (draft|accepted|active|current|archived|deprecated|past|discarded). For 'search': one value OR an array of up to 5 (e.g. ['active','accepted']).

label.description: For 'list': filter by label slug — matches entries across all collections.

cursor.description: For 'accountable': nextCursor of an earlier page.

mapEntryId.description: For 'gather': journey map entry ID for journey-aware context. Returns context organised by journey stage. Takes precedence over entryId when both are supplied. Example: '<PREFIX>-<n>'.

task.description: For 'gather': natural-language task description for loading task-relevant governance, binding constraints, and supporting context.

since.description: For 'changes': ISO 8601 timestamp — returns entries/relations modified since this time. For 'brief' briefType='delta': optional custom timestamp. Example: '2026-03-24T00:00:00Z'.

direction.description: For 'chain': 'outgoing' follows relations from source, 'incoming' to source (default outgoing). For 'find': incoming|outgoing|both (default both).

relationType.description: Relation type filter. For 'chain': optional filter to traverse only this relation type. For 'cross-cut': required — scans all relations of this type across the workspace. Examples: 'part_of', 'informs', 'governs', 'depends_on'.

mode.description: For gather: 'search' (default) or 'graph' (enhanced with provenance paths). Ignored when mapEntryId is provided.

maxHops.description: Relation traversal depth (1=direct only, 2=default, 3=wide net, 4=deep chain walk)

maxResults.description: Max entries to return in gather task mode (default 10)

strategy.description: Seed strategy for task-based gather: 'keyword' (FTS only, default) or 'hybrid' (vector + FTS). Only affects task mode.

skill.description: Skill name for 'incremental' action — identifies which skill's brief history to compare against. Examples: 'preflight', 'shaping', 'review'. Required when action is 'incremental'.

briefType.description: Compound query type for 'brief' action. 'steering': 7d changes + structural aggregation (part_of, depends_on, constrains) + incremental delta + workspace readiness. 'confidence': 7d changes + active bets summary (tensions: use the pb CLI's `tensions list`, not this action). 'delta': changes + relations since a custom timestamp (use 'since' param). Required when action is 'brief'.

templateId.description: For 'last-verified-brief': brief template identifier — currently 'steering-brief' is the only registered template.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: collections
tools.description:
Manage knowledge collections and workspace labels. Eleven actions:

- **list**: Browse all collections — glossary, business rules, tracking events, etc. Returns slug, name, description, and field schema. Use before capture to see what exists.
- **describe**: Full documentation for a single collection. Returns field help text, option decision guides, usage guidance, examples, and cross-references. Use when you need to understand a collection's purpose, field semantics, or option values.
- **update**: Update a collection's purpose, navGroup, fields, or (non-system only) stageLabelMap; its name, description, axis, status words and icon are the catalog's. Only provide the fields you want to change. Creating a NEW collection is not offered here — ask a platform admin to provision it, or enable the module ontology pack that owns the drawer.
- **audit**: Health report for all workspace collections. Checks classification metadata, displayHint coverage per field, and field schema gaps vs system definitions. Returns total collections, count with issues, and per-collection issue list.
- **export**: Full system_collection_definitions export as JSON. Includes all classification metadata (thinkingLayer, classificationPriority, classificationCheck, timelineRole, governanceRole, governanceFunction, etc.). Admin only.
- **label-list/label-create/label-update/label-delete/label-apply/label-remove**: manage workspace labels (absorbs the `labels` tool) — list all labels, create/update/delete a label, or apply/remove a label on an entry. Labels can be applied to any entry across any collection for cross-domain filtering.

action.description: 'list': browse all collections. 'update': update an existing collection. 'describe': full documentation for one collection — fields, option guides, usage guidance, examples. 'audit': health report for all collections — missing classification, displayHint coverage, and field schema gaps. 'export': full system_collection_definitions export with classification metadata (thinkingLayer, classificationPriority, classificationCheck, classificationSignals, governanceRole, governanceFunction, timelineRole, canBeElementOf, descriptionFieldKey). Admin only. 'label-list'/'label-create'/'label-update'/'label-delete'/'label-apply'/'label-remove': manage workspace labels (absorbs the `labels` tool). Creating a new collection is not offered here — ask a platform admin to provision it, or enable the module ontology pack that owns the drawer.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for create/update, e.g. 'glossary', 'tech-debt'. For label-*: label slug.

name.description: For label-*: the label's name. For update: refused (the catalog's).

description.description: For label-*: what the label means (max 2,000 chars). For update: refused (the catalog's).

purpose.description: Why this collection exists — strategic reason

icon.description: For update: always refused — a collection's icon comes from the platform catalog.

searchable.description: Whether this field is included in full-text search

displayHint.description: V2 rendering hint: how the field should be displayed in Cortex

zone.description: V2 layout zone: where the field appears in the entry view

colorMap.description: V2 value-to-semantic-color mapping, e.g. { critical: 'danger', low: 'success' }

accentSource.description: When true, this field's colorMap value drives the card-level accent styling

iconMap.description: Maps field values to icons (emoji/symbol), prepended to badge text

helpText.description: Help text shown in admin field editors

semanticRole.description: Semantic role for schema-driven consumers — enables field-key-independent validation and rendering

maxLength.description: Maximum character length for field values. Three-tier resolution: explicit > displayHint > type fallback.

minLength.description: Minimum character length for field values. Only explicit — no defaults.

fields.description: Field definitions for create, or replacement schema for update (replaces all fields)

axis.description: REQUIRED for create: 'work' (needs stageLabelMap + validWorkflowStatuses), 'none', or 'pending'. For update: always refused — a collection's axis comes from the platform catalog.

stageLabelMap.description: Required when axis is 'work': maps each valid workflowStatus to a canonical stage.

defaultCanonicalKey.description: The canonical_key entries in this collection default to (e.g. 'decision', 'insight'). Consumers read from collection doc; code map is fallback.

defaultWorkflowStatus.description: Default workflowStatus for new entries. For update: always refused — the status words come from the platform catalog.

validWorkflowStatuses.description: The allowed workflowStatus values for entries in this collection. For update: always refused — the status words come from the platform catalog.

classificationCheck.description: LLM decision-tree check for this collection (3–500 chars). Guides the classifier in routing entries here.

classificationPriority.description: Classifier priority (1–9, lower = higher priority). Used with classificationCheck to order the decision tree.

field.description: Entry data field key this criterion applies to, e.g. 'description', 'owner'

rule.description: 'required': field must be non-empty (blocks accept). 'min_length': minimum string length (warns). 'max_length': maximum string length (warns). 'pattern': regex match (warns).

value.description: For min_length/max_length: the length bound as a string integer. For pattern: the regex string. Unused for 'required'.

qualityCriteria.description: Per-collection accept gate rules. 'required' rule hard-blocks accepts on empty fields; 'min_length'/'pattern' rules warn. Pass an empty array to clear all criteria.

statusList.description: Ordered status vocabulary: {label, category, archiveDefault?}[]. For update: always refused — the status words come from the platform catalog.

parentSlug.description: For label-create: parent group slug for label hierarchy.

isGroup.description: For label-create/label-update: true if this is a group container, not a taggable label.

order.description: For label-create/label-update: sort order within its group.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: orient
tools.description:
Task-grounded context loader. Call `session action=start` first; it opens the session and hands you the briefing.

Pass `task` to load the governance and context for a specific task. Orient is advice for captures, relations, accepts, ticks and questions; workflow checkpoints and organisation-structure writes (membership, ownership, parent) still require an oriented session.

**tier** (action=task): Controls payload depth.
- `summary` (~10 KB) — compact, calibrated for task-scoped retrieval.
- `standard` (~256 KB) — rich, suited to workspace standups.
- `full` — complete payload, no cap. Use with deliberation.

The spine (vision, purpose, strategy highlights) is served in full and a grounding status flags when context was reduced.

Default: `standard`, with or without `task`. Explicit `tier` always wins.

**mode** (action=task): `full` (default) returns full context. `brief` returns compact summary — mapped to tier=summary internally.

action.description: 'task': task-grounded context loader, the only action.

mode.description: For 'task': full = full context (default). brief = compact summary for mid-session re-orientation. Prefer using the `tier` param for depth control.

tier.description: For 'task': payload depth. Defaults to standard (~256 KB), with or without a task. Pass summary, standard, or full to override.

task.description: For 'task': natural-language task description for task-scoped context. When provided, orient returns scored, relevant entries for the task.

changedPaths.description: Paths changed in the current working tree, if known (e.g. from a prior git status/diff tool call).

reviewedArtifactRefs.description: Chain entry IDs the caller has already reviewed this session, if tracked.

branchName.description: Current git branch name, if known.

startupSignals.description: For 'task': best-effort startup signals — changedPaths/reviewedArtifactRefs/branchName/worktreeName. All optional; omit fields you don't know.

invocationPath.description: For 'task': how this orient was invoked. Defaults to 'manual-orient' (the direct `orient task=...` call shape) when omitted.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: capture
tools.description:
The tool for creating a single knowledge entry. Creates an entry and returns a quality scorecard — all in one call. Provide a name and description; `collection` is optional — the kernel classifies when omitted and files a low-confidence pick as a draft with one line saying so. An agent capturing several atoms from one text calls this once per atom.

**Explicit data:** When you know the schema, pass `data: { field: value }` to set fields directly. A value in `data` is kept as sent; `description` is the entry's text and fills the collection's prose field only when `data` leaves it empty (the same rule as `pb capture`); when `data` carries the prose field, `description` and `context` are used for classification and judging only and are not stored. Governance entries also require a top-level `why`.

**Compound capture:** Pass `links` to create relations in the same call; a capture writes no other relations. A capture lands as a `draft` to accept with `entries action=accept`; a question is born open. The reply names possible duplicates; only an exact name in the collection is refused.

collection.description: Collection slug, e.g. 'tensions', 'rules', 'glossary', 'decisions'. Optional — the kernel classifies when omitted.

context.description: Optional additional context; appended to the description, so it is stored only when the description is (not when data carries the prose field).

canonicalKey.description: Semantic type (e.g. 'decision', 'tension', 'vision'). Auto-assigned from collection if omitted.

data.description: Explicit field values; user-provided wins over inferred.

type.description: Relation type. The spine links: A work package validates an accepted key result. A key result hangs on an accepted objective with part_of. An objective hangs on an accepted strategy with part_of. A strategy hangs on an accepted vision with part_of. A vision hangs on an accepted purpose with part_of.

links.description: Links written with the entry in one transaction; each returns written or refused with a reason; a refused link fails nothing.

sourceRef.description: URI or path of the source document backing this entry.

sourceExcerpt.description: Verbatim excerpt from the source backing this entry's claims.

suggestOnly.description: suggestOnly was removed: call capture with preview: true to check a capture without writing.

ownerRoleEntryId.description: Owning role (rung-2); you must hold it; its team is the one you hold it in (root first, else the shallowest).

team.description: For a role: the team it is born in. For a team: its parent team. Entry ID or ref; defaults to the root team.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: quality
tools.description:
Assess, re-evaluate, and verify entry/work package quality. Four actions:

- **check**: Read the entry's server quality verdict (tier + criteria) — it does not re-score.
- **re-evaluate**: Trigger a fresh quality evaluation. Returns heuristic verdict immediately, schedules LLM evaluation in background.
- **verify-chain**: Verify knowledge entries against the actual codebase (codeMapping drift, cross-references) — absorbs `verify`. Produces a trust report with a trust score.
- **spine-check**: Structural completeness of the purpose+vision+strategy spine — duplicate singletons, connectedness, per-strategy refusal heuristic; story:true also runs the on-demand one-story LLM judgment (never scheduled, result labelled [unvalidated]). Async: a plain call reads back the latest stored verdict and auto-schedules a new run ONLY when none is already in flight AND the stored one is absent/stale/missing the requested story pass — repeated polling never re-triggers work. Pass refresh:true to force a fresh run regardless.

action.description: 'check': read the entry's server quality verdict (tier + criteria). 're-evaluate': trigger fresh evaluation. 'verify-chain': verify entries against the codebase (codeMapping drift, cross-references) — absorbs `verify`. 'spine-check': structural completeness of the purpose+vision+strategy spine — story:true also runs the on-demand one-story judgment.

collection.description: For 'verify-chain': collection slug to verify (default: glossary).

mode.description: For 'verify-chain': 'report' = read-only trust report (default). 'fix' = also update drifted codeMapping statuses.

story.description: For 'spine-check': also run the on-demand one-story LLM judgment (never scheduled; result labelled [unvalidated]).

refresh.description: For 'spine-check': force a new run even if a fresh verdict already exists. Default false — a plain call NEVER re-triggers work just to read the last result; it auto-schedules only when no run is already in flight AND the stored verdict is absent/stale/missing the requested story pass.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: workflows
tools.description:
Chainwork workflow discovery, start/resume, checkpointing, and run inspection. Four actions:

- **list**: Browse available workflows — retro, shape-a-bet, implementation-review, process-change.
- **start**: Start or resume a workflow. Call with workflowId (e.g. 'implementation-review', 'retro', 'shape', 'process-change'). Returns the first (or current) round instructions and the exact checkpoint call to use when the round is complete. Use this when the user says 'run implementation review', 'run retro', 'shape this', or 'process change' — it is the tool entry point for running a workflow.
- **checkpoint**: Record a round's output. Persists progress. At completion, some workflows support isFinal=true to create the summary chain entry.
- **get-run**: Inspect a persisted workflow run by run ID or by workflow ID in the current session.

action.description: 'list': browse available workflows. 'start': start or resume a workflow — returns first (or current) round and next-step checkpoint call. 'checkpoint': record round output or final summary. 'get-run': inspect a persisted workflow run.

workflowId.description: Workflow ID for start, checkpoint, or get-run, e.g. 'retro', 'implementation-review'

runId.description: Workflow run ID: for get-run, which run to load; for checkpoint, target this run (avoids session drift — pass runId from get-run).

output.description: The round's output — either legacy synthesized text or a typed workflow run payload.

isFinal.description: If true, finalize an existing durable workflow run from its terminal round and create the summary chain entry.

restart.description: If true, start a new durable run from the workflow's first round in the current session.

summaryName.description: Optional name for final chain entry. If omitted, the workflow summary template is used.

summaryDescription.description: Optional override for the final chain entry description. Defaults to the final round output text.

summaryEntryId.description: Link an existing entry as the run's summary instead of creating one. Used by facilitated workflows (e.g. shape) where the primary record is created by the specialized tool.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: workspace
tools.description:
Diagnostics, session identity, and usage for the current workspace. Six actions:

- **check**: Verify connectivity — workspace, collections, entries, latency.
- **whoami**: Session identity — workspace ID, slug, name.
- **status**: Workspace readiness — checks (pass/fail), gaps, stats (entries, relations, orphans).
- **audit**: Session audit log — last N backend calls with summary.
- **self-test**: Validate all registered tool schemas.
- **usage**: LLM usage and cost summary — spend, tokens, model/feature breakdown.

action.description: 'check': connectivity and workspace stats. 'whoami': session identity. 'status': workspace readiness. 'audit': session audit log. 'self-test': validate all tool schemas. 'usage': LLM usage and cost summary.

limit.description: For 'audit': how many recent calls to show (max 50, default 20).

periodDays.description: For 'usage': number of days to look back (default 30, max 90).

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Submit Product Brain feedback from any agent, including with a read-only key and no session. list reads back your own workspace's feedback (all statuses, no gate). Vendor operators can also queue (triage), note, group, and change queue status.

action.description: submit requires message; list returns your own workspace's feedback (all statuses); queue is the vendor triage queue (system admins only) and accepts filters; note requires feedbackId+note; group requires feedbackIds+groupId (null clears); status requires feedbackId+status and may carry tensionId and answer.

message.description: Required for submit: the product feedback text (max 10,000 characters).

category.description: Submit/queue category; submit defaults to other.

command.description: Optional submit command context; argument values are scrubbed server-side.

feedbackId.description: Required for note/status: target feedback ID.

feedbackIds.description: Required for group: 1–100 target feedback IDs.

note.description: Required for note: replacement triage note (max 4,000 characters).

status.description: list/queue filter (any status, including 'screening'); the status action's required target value excludes 'screening' (system-only).

tensionId.description: status only: the tension the report joined, its display id TEN- and a number (vendor-only, never shown to the reporter).

answer.description: status only: the one sentence the reporter reads under their report, dated (max 240 characters).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous list/queue response (continueCursor); omit for the first page.

full.description: list/queue only: return untruncated messages; allowed only when limit <= 5.

tools.name: question
tools.description:
Routed questions — a question is born with no owner and escalates straight to the team lead; the team lead reassigns it to a role. Five actions:

- **create**: create a new routed question from text. Always born escalated to the team lead — there is no domain-owner suggestion any more.
- **assign**: reassign ownership to a role (`toRole` required — no self-confirm, no person-only reassignment).
- **answer**: close the loop. Writes `text` on the question as its answer, or links an existing decision via `answerEntryId` — never both.
- **force-close**: Team-Lead-only escape hatch (reason required) for a question that cannot otherwise be resolved.
- **list**: the ack-gate read model — what you owe (`mine:false`, the default), or (`mine:true`) every question you asked, including closed ones, with its outcome.

`blocks` (repeatable, on create) records what a question is holding up — pass entry ids it blocks.

action.description: 'create': create a new routed question from text — the dedicated birth action; every question is born escalated to the team lead (generic entry creation and move-and-retype also pair a routing facet). 'assign': reassign ownership to a role (toRole required — no bare self-confirm, no toPerson). 'answer': close the loop — writes the answer on the question and moves it to answered; --entry links an existing decision instead. 'force-close': Team-Lead-only escape hatch — reason required. 'list': the ack-gate read model — what you owe (or, with mine:true, every question you asked, including closed ones).

entryId.description: Target question's id (human TEN-nnn form or a raw entry id). Required for every action except 'create'/'list'.

text.description: 'create': the question text. 'answer': the answer text (mutually exclusive with answerEntryId, max 2000 chars).

blocks.description: 'create': entry ids this question is blocking (repeatable).

toRole.description: 'assign': reassign to this role (human ROL-nnn form or a raw entry id) — required.

answerEntryId.description: 'answer': point at an already-written entry instead of supplying text (mutually exclusive with text).

mine.description: 'list': true for arm C (every question YOU asked, every status). Omit/false for the ack-gate view (what you owe).

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: role
tools.description:
Workspace roles — who holds a role and where it sits. Five actions:

- **seat**: put a person in this role, by person id or email, or by `newPersonName` for someone with no login yet (a placeholder person, created once per exact name). The role's home team is used; name `teamId` only for Team Lead. A held role refuses a second holder and names the holder; the person keeps their other roles in the team. Needs the team's Team Lead. With `onMyAuthority`, the team's Team Lead seats a second Team Lead on their own authority; unseating them revokes it.
- **unseat**: take this role from a person; their other roles in the team stay. The last active Team Lead of a team is refused. Invite a person, or take them out of a team, with the `people` tool.
- **release_move** / **accept_move** / **refuse_move**: move a role or team (`childId`) to a team whose Team Lead is another seat. Acting as Team Lead of its current team, release it toward `teamId`; acting as Team Lead of that team, accept it, or refuse it with `why` (it stays, and a tension goes to its current team's Team Lead).

Read what a role owns with `context action=accountable`.

action.description: 'seat': put a person in this role. 'unseat': take this role from a person. 'release_move' / 'accept_move' / 'refuse_move': move a role or team to a team with another Team Lead.

roleId.description: The role, by the human chain id `chain.getEntry` or `pb get` would print for it, or a raw entry id.

person.description: 'seat' / 'unseat': an existing person, by person id or exact email. For 'seat', give this or newPersonName, not both.

newPersonName.description: 'seat': the name of a person who has no login yet; a placeholder person is created once and reused for the same exact name. Refused when the name belongs to someone with an account.

teamId.description: 'seat' / 'unseat': the team, by chain id or entry id. Only needed for Team Lead, which lives in every team; any other role is seated in its home team. 'release_move': the team it moves to.

onMyAuthority.description: 'seat', Team Lead only: as the team's Team Lead, seat a second Team Lead who holds the seat on your authority until you unseat them.

childId.description: 'release_move' / 'accept_move' / 'refuse_move': the role or team that moves, by chain id or entry id.

why.description: 'refuse_move': why the move is refused; it becomes a tension for the old team's Team Lead.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: people
tools.description:
People in the workspace. Two actions:

- **invite**: send a login link to `email`. Give `person` (a placeholder's id, as `role action=seat` printed it) to invite that person in place: they keep every role they hold. Or give `newPersonName` to invite someone new. A person who already has a login or an invite is refused. Needs a workspace owner or admin.
- **remove**: take `person` out of the team `teamId`; every role they hold there goes with it. To take one role, use `role action=unseat`. Needs the team's Team Lead.

action.description: 'invite': send a login link by email. 'remove': take a person out of a team.

email.description: 'invite': where the login link goes. Required for 'invite'.

person.description: 'invite': a placeholder's person id, instead of newPersonName. 'remove': the person, by person id or exact email.

newPersonName.description: 'invite': the name of a new person to invite, instead of person.

teamId.description: 'remove': the team, by chain id or entry id. Required for 'remove'.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

tools.name: outcome
tools.description:
Key-result outcomes: record the measured readings behind a number.

- **record**: Record a reading — evidence, not a verdict; any connector may record one.

Read with the read-only `context` tool: `context action=outcome entryId="..."` (the derived view, its objective and sibling key results), `context action=readings entryId="..."` (the readings).

action.description: 'record': record a reading (evidence, not a verdict). Reads live on context: action=outcome and action=readings.

entryId.description: The key result (or other outcome-bearing) entry, by its chain id. Required.

valueText.description: 'record': verbatim as-reported form when the source was not clean, e.g. '~62%'. Display only.

asOf.description: 'record': when the world was in this state, as a parseable date (default: now). Back-dating a backfill is legitimate — it shows up as asOf earlier than recordedAt.

correctsReadingId.description: 'record': required with kind='correction' — the reading id this replaces. Refused if that row is already superseded.

recordedByRoleId.description: 'record': the accountable role (default: the entry's reporterRoleId, then its owning role).

note.description: 'record': free-text note recorded with the reading.

source.description: 'record': where the number came from — a dashboard name, a query, a URL.

sessionId.description: The sessionId `session action=start` returned. Pass it on every write: the connection does not remember your session between calls.

instructions:
Product Brain (PB) is the single source of truth for your team's product knowledge: decisions, tensions, rules, work and the links between them.

## What session start hands you

Call `session action=start` first. The reply names:
- the workspace and the role you act as;
- notices, including open questions routed to you;
- the rule lists that bind you, each rule as one sentence with its why, its owner role and, when it has one, its date.

Read those rules before you propose or build. If the work conflicts with one, stop, name the rule and ask the user before going on. Never design around a rule.

## Pull the rest

- `orient action=task task="<what you are doing>"`: context shaped to the task, with the rules for your team and role.
- `context action=get entryId="<ID>"`: one entry in full, with data, relations and history.
- `context action=search query="<noun>"`: find entries by what they are about.

## Writing

Write actions (capture, entries update and accept, relations create, batch-create and delete, people invite and remove, role seat and unseat) need an active session and a readwrite key.
Pass the `sessionId` that `session action=start` returned on every write: the connection does not remember it.
Use `capture` to create an entry and read its reply: it lands as a draft, except a question, which is born open and needs no `entries action=accept`.
Link entries with `relations action=create` — a relation is written only when you ask, with exactly the verb you send.
Spine links run child to parent, each part_of the level above.
A work package validates a key result; informs joins no levels.
Before accepting a spine entry, preflight it: it names what blocks.
Finish with `session action=wrapup-review`, then `session action=close`.
If the work falls outside the active work packages, name the gap and ask the user before designing it.
